title.title: Random walk in random environment: escape implies speed
title.subtitle: Claim: in $d \ge 2$, a walk in an iid uniformly elliptic environment that escapes in a direction has positive speed

beats.text: In one dimension, traps let a walk escape to infinity at zero speed (curves schematic)
Conjecture: in $d \ge 2$, escaping in a direction $\ell$ forces positive speed
Claim: proved for iid uniformly elliptic environments, every $d \ge 2$

plain: A walker on a grid of randomly tilted floor tiles: if it drifts away, must it drift at a steady speed?

steps: Cut the path at moments it never drops back below a new record
Show each piece lasts a finite time on average
Stitched together, the pieces give a steady positive speed

voice.text: In one dimension traps let a walker escape at zero speed. Not in two or more?
Cut the path at record moments; each piece has finite average length.
Claimed: escaping forces a positive speed.
